title: Solving Problems: Money, Rate and Ratio
seo_title: Grade 4 Money, Rate and Ratio Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_text: Solve problems in contexts involving whole numbers, including financial contexts, measurement contexts, comparing two or more quantities of the same kind (ratio), comparing two quantities of different kinds (rate), and grouping and equal sharing with remainders.
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 4 money worksheets: rand and cents, shopping and change, rates such as rand per kilogram, and sharing in a ratio. 100 questions with memos.
key_sub: Rate: R18 per kg, so 3 kg costs 3 × R18.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • R1 = 100c. R12,50 is 12 rand and 50 cents, or 1 250c.
  • To find the cost of several items, multiply; then add. Change = money paid − cost.
  • A rate compares two different things: R18 per kilogram. For 3 kg, pay 3 × R18.
  • A ratio compares parts: for every 1 sweet Thabo gets, Lerato gets 2.

Examples

Example

3 kg of apples at R24 per kg; pay with R100

3 × R24 = R72

R100 − R72

Answer: R28 change

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
R2,50 as 25cR2,50 = 250c.
Cost instead of changeSubtract the cost from the money paid.
Sharing equallyUse the ratio, not halves.

faq.q: What does CAPS Grade 4 say about problem solving?
faq.a: Solve problems in contexts involving money, measurement and comparing two or more quantities of the same kind (ratio) and of different kinds (rate), and grouping and equal sharing.

faq.q: How do we write rand and cents?
faq.a: R12,50: rand, then a comma, then the cents.

faq.q: What is the difference between rate and ratio?
faq.a: A ratio compares the same kind of thing; a rate compares different kinds.
